{{short description|American mathematician}}
{{use mdy dates|date=January 2021}}

'''Shahriar Shahriari''' (born May 30, 1956) is an American mathematician. He is the William Polk Russell Professor of Mathematics at [[Pomona College]].<ref name="Official">{{cite web |title=Shahriar Shahriari |url=https://www.pomona.edu/directory/people/shahriar-shahriari |publisher=Pomona College |access-date=18 January 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Shahriari was born on May 30, 1956, in [[Tehran, Iran]], to Parviz and Zomorod Shahriari.<ref name="Encyclopedia.com">{{cite web |title=Shahriari, Shahriar 1956- |url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/arts/educational-magazines/shahriari-shahriar-1956 |publisher=[[Encyclopedia.com]] |access-date=18 January 2021}}</ref> He attended [[Oberlin College]], graduating in 1977, and subsequently received his doctorate from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] in 1986.<ref name="Official"/>

==Career==
Shahriari began teaching at [[Pomona College]] in 1989.<ref name="Official"/> In 2006, he published a [[calculus]] textbook titled ''Approximately Calculus''.<ref name="Approximately review">{{cite journal |last1=Bressoud |first1=David |title=Review |journal=[[The American Mathematical Monthly]] |date=2013 |volume=120 |issue=6 |pages=577–580 |doi=10.4169/amer.math.monthly.120.06.577 |s2cid=218543048 |issn=0002-9890}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 1998, Shahriari shared the [[Carl B. Allendoerfer Award]] with Dan Kalman and Robert Mena for their paper "Variations on an irrational theme—Geometry, dynamics, algebra".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/writing-awards/carl-b-allendoerfer-awards|title=Carl B. Allendoerfer Awards|publisher=Mathematical Association of America|access-date=2021-01-19|archive-date=July 22, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200722154753/https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/writing-awards/carl-b-allendoerfer-awards|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2015, he received a [[Mathematical Association of America]] [[Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award for Distinguished Teaching in Mathematics]].<ref name="Official"/>
